fieldValues.title: Field identity rules: enforce in schema, enforce in a validator, or stop claiming them (srs#236)
fieldValues.decision_question: For each documented Field identity rule (snake_case name, reserved / and @, reserved core namespace, uuid and date-time formats), do we enforce it in field.json, in an engine validator, or stop claiming it as normative?
fieldValues.context:
Problem: the spec states Field identity rules as normative prose and field.json enforces none of them; format assertion is off in srs-schema, so id: "f-1" validates.
Why it matters: / and @ are the reference separators (namespace/name@version); a name containing them makes references ambiguous. Documented conventions that are not enforced bind nobody (SP-01).
Options and consequences: (a) pattern constraints in field.json plus format assertion on: strongest, but tightens a normative schema and may break existing instances and engine fixtures. (b) keep the schema loose, enforce in an engine validator with a diagnostic code: no schema change, but independent implementers still miss the rules. (c) drop the claims from the spec: honest, weakens the guarantee. (d) do nothing.
Recommendation: audit all existing Field instances first (read-only), then (a) for name and namespace where the audit is clean, with a validator and diagnostic code for the core reservation.
Action needed: rule on the option; the change is Door 2/3 (normative schema), so the builder cannot proceed without it.
Urgency: the issue is P0 and blocks-gate.
fieldValues.friction: srs#236 is the top ready item in WG Third-party ready, but it names no ruling and changes conformance rules and docs/schema/2.0, which the builder mandate excludes.
fieldValues.alternatives_considered:
(a) Enforce in field.json (pattern plus format assertion), after an audit.
(b) Enforce in an engine validator only.
(c) Stop claiming the rules normatively.
(d) Do nothing.
fieldValues.key_requirements: Audit existing instances before tightening; a deprecation story if violations exist; engine fixtures conform; schema mirrors re-synced.
fieldValues.decision_statement: Audit first, then enforce name and namespace rules in field.json with format assertion on, and the core reservation in a validator with a diagnostic code; carried as an RFC or RFC revision.
fieldValues.rationale: Documented conventions are enforced conventions; the separators are load-bearing for references.
fieldValues.revisit_when: The audit finds existing violations, or the RFC is drafted.
fieldValues.next_steps: On ruling: a read-only audit issue, then the RFC (Door 2) or revision (Door 3).
